findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post footer enables stored XSS
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends `#{url}` to the contents without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with cook_method raw_html, so cooked == raw with no sanitization. The `url` reaches this code from the user-controlled `embed_url` query parameter (EmbedController#best -> RetrieveTopic job -> TopicRetriever -> import_remote). TopicRetriever only checks that the URI host equals embeddable_host; the path may contain `'` (a legal URI character), so a value such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` injects an attribute into the anchor. If the embeddable host serves any 200 page for that path, the payload is stored in a public post authored by the embed_by user and executes for every forum visitor and in the embed iframe. The url (and the title) must be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

findings.title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized
findings.body: Posts created by TopicEmbed.import use `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for that method, bypassing PrettyText sanitization entirely. For the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed) the content is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` with no filtering at all, and for import_remote Readability's tag whitelist still allows `<a href>` with arbitrary schemes (e.g. javascript:). A compromised or malicious feed/source therefore yields stored script injection rendered to all users (best.html.erb outputs `raw post.cooked`). Imported HTML should be passed through the sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize/PrettyText whitelist) before being stored.

findings.title: `i.content.scrub` raises for standard RSS items and on Ruby < 2.1
findings.body: SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom feeds; plain RSS 2.0 items expose `description` (and `content_encoded` for the content module), so `i.content` is nil for most RSS feeds and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll (retry: false). Additionally, `String#scrub` only exists from Ruby 2.1; on Ruby 2.0 (current at the time of this code) it raises NoMethodError even for Atom feeds. Fall back to `i.content_encoded || i.description` and guard the encoding cleanup.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The code then strips all leading slashes and prepends the prefix, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is a broken link/image. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed content and Readability output. Use `URI.join(url, href)` or skip hrefs beginning with `//`.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of equality
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For `discourseUrl = "http://discourse.example.com/"` an attacker page at `http://discourse.example.co` (a prefix) passes the check. The impact is limited to controlling the iframe height, but the check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl for equality with e.origin.

findings.title: open-uri fetch of user-influenced URL follows redirects with no timeout (SSRF)
findings.body: `open(url).read` uses Kernel#open/open-uri on a URL derived from the `embed_url` request parameter. Only the host is validated; open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable host (or anyone who can place a redirect on it) can make the Sidekiq worker fetch arbitrary internal URLs. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge response ties up the worker. Use an HTTP client with redirect disabled or re-validated, timeouts, and a response size cap.

findings.title: Every cache-miss embed request runs a full synchronous feed poll
findings.body: perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when feed polling is enabled. This downloads and imports the entire RSS feed (creating/revising posts for every item) on each embed request whose URL has no TopicEmbed yet. The 60 s throttle is per embed_url and is bypassed for staff, so distinct URLs (or a staff member) can trigger repeated full feed imports on the worker and heavy writes to the database.

findings.title: setnx followed by separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key
findings.body: The throttle does `$redis.setnx(key)` and then `$redis.expire(key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the worker dies or redis errors between them, the key is created without a TTL and that embed_url is throttled forever for non-staff users (the topic never gets retrieved). Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or setex-style atomic operation).

findings.title: Concurrent imports of the same URL hit the unique index after creating a topic
findings.body: import checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later `TopicEmbed.create!`. The hourly PollFeed job and a RetrieveTopic job (which itself invokes PollFeed) can import the same URL concurrently; the second one creates a topic and post, then `create!` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on the unique embed_url index, rolling back the transaction and propagating an exception that aborts the rest of the feed import. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path.

findings.title: Rails 3 lockfile not updated for new gems
findings.body: ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock, but the Rails 3 lockfile (Gemfile.lock, used when RAILS3 is set) is not updated. In deployment/frozen mode Bundler will refuse to boot in Rails 3 mode until the lockfile is regenerated, and the gems will be missing at runtime for `require 'simple-rss'` / `require 'ruby-readability'`.

findings.title: Already-committed migration modified to add force: true
findings.body: An existing migration is edited to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Editing a migration that has already been applied elsewhere is unsafe: anyone who re-runs it (e.g. via `db:migrate:redo` or a fresh schema rebuild from migrations) will have the existing top_topics table silently dropped along with its data. The same `force: true` is used in the new topic_embeds migration; a new migration should not need it.

findings.title: Stray `end if` in ERB only compiles by accident
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` emits the Ruby `end if` with no condition; it only parses because ERB appends the next template text as `@output_buffer.safe_append=...` on the following line, which becomes the modifier-if condition. Any reformatting (e.g. putting another `<% %>` tag directly after, or a different ERB handler) turns this into a SyntaxError and the embed page will 500. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Loading page reloads forever and re-enqueues a job on every reload
findings.body: The loading view reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely. Each reload hits EmbedController#best, which, while no TopicEmbed exists, enqueues another RetrieveTopic job. If retrieval permanently fails (invalid host, 404, user not configured), every open embed on the page will keep polling and enqueuing Sidekiq jobs with no backoff or stop condition.
